final_candidates.decision_summary: N301 is the V3-loop high-mannose glycan at the N301/N332 immunodominant face, a documented contact for V3-glycan bNAbs. Deleting it is a plausible escape route with tolerable fitness cost in BG505.

The N300 sequon forms an alternate glycan site at the V3 base that can compensate for N301 loss; its removal may further blunt glycan-dependent bNAb binding. Confidence limited by redundant glycan occupancy patterns.
N337 is a V3-stem glycan contributing to antibody access in the V3 region; deletion may reduce glycan/V3-directed antibody binding. Its peripheral variable-loop location keeps folding risk moderate.

stop_reason.detail: Self-review has converged on the Top-3 glycan-deletion escape candidates and no external evidence is available to refine them further.

history.rationale: Removing the N301 glycan perturbs V3-glycan bnAb epitopes (e.g., 10-1074 class) with partial compensation by adjacent glycans preserving fitness.

N301 (HXB2 N332) is the V3-loop glycan central to PGT121/PGT128 recognition; removing the sequon is a well-characterized escape route in BG505. Some fitness cost is expected from glycan loss, hence moderate confidence.
N301 is the V3-loop high-mannose glycan at the 'N301/N332' immunodominant face and is a well-documented bNAb contact; its loss is a plausible escape route with tolerable fitness cost in BG505.

The adjacent N300 forms an alternate glycan site in the NNNT sequon at the V3 base and can partially compensate for N301 loss; its removal could further blunt glycan-dependent bNAb binding. Lower confidence due to redundant glycan occupancy patterns.
Adjacent sequon glycan can shift occupancy; removing it may destabilize residual glycan shielding of the V3 base after N301 loss, but compensatory occupancy patterns lower confidence.

N337 (NET at 337-339) is a V3-stem glycan contributing to antibody access in the V3 region; deletion may reduce binding of glycan/V3-directed antibodies. Position is in a variable loop, so folding risk is moderate.
V3-stem glycan near the base contributes to glycan-dependent antibody recognition; slight upward adjustment because it is structurally peripheral and likely folding-tolerant.
N275 is a conserved C2-region glycan near the CD4bs/loop D; deletion has been reported to reduce VRC01-class sensitivity. However, proximity to conserved structures raises folding/fitness risk.
N275 removal reduces VRC01-class CD4bs sensitivity, but its conservation near loop D raises fitness risk; modest raise as CD4bs escape is a distinct, valuable escape axis.
N184 lies in the V1/V2 region, and altering V2 glycans can affect apex-directed bNAbs. High structural sensitivity of the apex trimer makes this risky for folding and fitness.
V2-apex glycan edits can reduce apex bNAb binding but trimer-apex structural sensitivity keeps confidence low.

N135 is a V1-loop glycan site; V1 glycan changes are a known general escape axis with often-acceptable fitness costs. Low confidence because no specific antibody target at this site in BG505 is recalled.
No specific antibody-recallable target at N135 in BG505; V1 glycan removal is speculative and unlikely to outperform the V3-base glycan deletions.

rejection.reason: No specific antibody-recallable target at N135 in BG505; V1 glycan removal is speculative and unlikely to outperform the V3-base glycan deletions.
